claim: CodeVetter can capture bounded request-scoped Node trace activity, normalize closed libuv worker and V8 mechanisms, and use compatible libuv activity to choose a narrower probe without presenting elapsed overlap as CPU attribution or granting edit authority.

controlled_proofs: An actual pbkdf2 HTTP handler produces a complete crypto libuv worker interval and routes to inspect_libuv_threadpool_crypto.
Overlapping intervals are unioned within each mechanism and across each public activity group rather than summed as CPU.
Live partial trace containers admit only complete event objects; malformed, oversized, unpaired, truncated, contaminated, and incompatible evidence fails closed.
Trace arguments, raw event names, event IDs, process IDs, thread IDs, paths, versions, values, and absolute timestamps do not enter public evidence.
Native activity routes remain source-null, low-confidence, edit-ineligible, and contain no activity-to-CPU ratio or subtraction.

real_product_evidence.interpretation: The real replay proves exact-request collection and privacy-bounded normalization. Its libuv activity remained below the fixed 5 ms routing floor, so it does not establish a libuv bottleneck or optimization.

limitations: Trace activity is elapsed overlap and may execute concurrently; it is not exclusive CPU time and is never subtracted from or divided by process CPU.
The trace observer changes the diagnostic request and therefore does not replace uninstrumented paired benchmark evidence.
The selected categories do not cover every native addon, V8 background task, child process, kernel operation, or external service.
The runtime disables repository Next configuration and does not establish production-build equivalence.
The existing browser assertion failed, so the evidence authorizes no source edit, optimization, correctness, or production claim.
